test_title: PYST 4: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - English Language (Held On 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Change the following from active to passive:

Legal analysts had consistently scrutinized the wording of the statute since its inception.

options.text: The wording of the statute had been consistently scrutinized by legal analysts since its inception.
The statute wording was being scrutinized since its inception by analysts.
Legal wording had been scrutinized by legal analysts since its inception.
The wording had been under scrutiny by legal analysts since its inception.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Passive Voice Transformation:** To convert a sentence from active to passive, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The original sentence is in the **Past Perfect Tense** (Active: *had + past participle*).
 
• The structure for **Past Perfect Passive** is: **Object + had + been + Past Participle + (by + Subject)**.
 
• **Sentence Breakdown:** 
 
 
• **Active Subject:** Legal analysts
 
• **Active Verb:** had consistently scrutinized
 
• **Active Object:** the wording of the statute
 
 
 
• In the passive version, "The wording of the statute" moves to the front, and "had scrutinized" becomes "had been scrutinized." The adverb "consistently" remains between the auxiliary verbs.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The wording of the statute had been consistently scrutinized by legal analysts since its inception."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "The statute wording was being scrutinized..." – This uses the **Past Continuous Passive** tense, which changes the original meaning.
 
• **Option 3:** "Legal wording had been scrutinized..." – This inaccurately changes the specific object "the wording of the statute" to a generalized "legal wording."
 
• **Option 4:** "The wording had been under scrutiny..." – This uses a prepositional phrase ("under scrutiny") instead of the passive verb form of the specific verb "scrutinized."
